chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi from Ubays ibn Hisham from Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Minqari from Hisham Al-Saydani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked him about this Verse: 'The people of Nuh and the dwellers of Ar-Rass rejected (prophets) before them.' So he (peace be upon him) said with his hand, 'Like this,' and he wiped one of them with the other, and he said: 'Hunna al-lawati bi al-lawati,' meaning women with women.

key_terms.الرَّسِّ: Ar-Rass (a place or people mentioned in the Quran, often associated with Thamud or a specific location)
key_terms.اللَّوَاتِي: Al-lawati (a plural form used here to denote women, specifically in the context of lesbianism)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'Al-lawati' mean in the context of the people of Nuh?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the Quranic term 'Al-lawati' by gesturing with his hands, indicating a specific reference to lesbianism (women engaging with women), thereby linking it to the sins of the people of Nuh and Ar-Rass. This narration is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the distinct category of female homosexuality, often discussed alongside male sodomy in legal texts. The gesture serves as a hermeneutical key, emphasizing the physical nature of the act described in the Quranic narrative of divine punishment.
